# Ryan Burke

> Ryan Burke is a software engineer, film photographer, oil pastel painter, basketball junkie, and twenty-two-handicap golfer. Also: Frank Ocean listener and Diddy Kong main. This is Ryan's personal site.

## About

Ryan is a senior software engineer living on the US east coast who architects thoughtfully-designed software systems. Outside of work: basketball, film photography, oil pastels, golf (not well), and chilling out with Ryan's dog and wife.

- [About](https://rburke.dev/#about)

## Experience

### Professional summary

Senior Software Engineer with nearly six years of experience designing scalable distributed systems and cloud-native applications. At DealerOn, Ryan helps build a greenfield website editor and rendering platform, co-led the split of the company's largest monolith into six independently owned services, and led the migration of its mission-critical Leads platform to three deployable services. Ryan focuses on reliable architecture, clear service contracts, and mentoring engineers.

### Senior Software Engineer at DealerOn (Oct 2025 – Present)

Tech: .NET, C#, TypeScript, Vue.js, Azure, SQL, RabbitMQ, Redis, Claude, .NET Aspire, Docker, Microservices, Distributed Systems, REST APIs, Resilience Patterns

Full-stack engineer with six years of experience architecting scalable distributed systems and cloud-native applications for the automotive industry. Proven track record of leading architectural initiatives, improving system reliability, and mentoring engineers.

- Develop a greenfield drag-and-drop page editor and rendering platform that lets automotive dealerships build, customize, and publish websites, working across frontend, backend, and cross-service integrations.
- Design versioned API and data contracts for an extensible widget architecture, allowing other teams to integrate independently developed components through shared NuGet packages while preserving backward compatibility.
- Improve frontend performance and reliability with non-blocking CSS, client-side caching, Grafana dashboards, and automated alerts.

### Software Engineer at DealerOn (Feb 2021 – Oct 2025)

- Co-led the decomposition of the company's largest monolith into six independently owned services, defining service boundaries, data migration strategies, and CI/CD workflows while coordinating work across engineering teams.
- Led the Leads platform migration to three independently deployable microservices using incremental migration, isolated databases, and durable RabbitMQ messaging.
- Improved platform uptime to 99.7% and reduced severity incidents by 30% through service isolation, fault-tolerant messaging, retry policies, and graceful degradation.
- Served as a technical subject matter expert for architecture decisions, design reviews, technical roadmaps, and code reviews, while mentoring fellow engineers.

### nCov-19 Genome Variant (project on GitHub)

Tech: C, Dynamic Programming, Burrows-Wheeler Transform, Suffix Arrays, FM-Index

Seed-search tool used to compare read-variants to the nCov-19 virus genome using the Burrows-Wheeler transform, suffix arrays, the FM-Index, and core dynamic programming principles.

- [Repository](https://github.com/RyanDBurke/coronavirus-genome-variant)

### Technical skills

- Languages: C#, SQL, TypeScript
- Frameworks: .NET, .NET Aspire, Vue.js
- Cloud & infrastructure: Microsoft Azure, Docker, Redis, FusionCache
- Messaging: RabbitMQ, MassTransit
- Architecture & practices: Microservices, distributed systems, REST APIs, SQL Server, database design, CI/CD, resilience patterns

- [Experience](https://rburke.dev/#experience)

## Bean

Bean is Ryan's dog, a gray-and-tan French bulldog. This section shows only an interactive 3D voxel model of Bean, built from his original pixel-art sprite. He turns his head to look at the viewer, breathes and wags his tail. Drag sideways to rotate him.

- [Bean](https://rburke.dev/#bean)

## Film

Ryan shoots film. The site shows a row of Ryan's film photos that drifts sideways on its own and can be dragged to browse, including portraits, a couple's shoot, an engagement shoot on the Brooklyn Bridge and in the rain in the West Village, a paddleboarder at sunset, a summer evening at a park pond, and travel shots from Arizona, France, Madrid, Sevilla, and a sunset swim in La Romana. Tapping a photo flips it over to show its title and the camera and film it was shot on (for example a Bronica SQ-A with Portra 800, a Fuji GA645zi, a Nikon L35AF, or an Olympus XA).

- [Film](https://rburke.dev/#photography)

## Golf

Ryan's personal-best golf rounds, each one breaking the last. The current best is 93, shot on July 15, 2026 at Laytonsville (par 71): 45 on the front nine and 48 on the back. The site shows its hole-by-hole scorecard: front 5, 4, 5, 7, 3, 6, 4, 6, 5; back 6, 6, 5, 4, 5, 6, 5, 4, 7. Earlier personal bests: 96 at Laytonsville (April 19, 2026), 100 at Needwood (March 8, 2026), 108 at Northwest Park (January 12, 2026), 111 at Fairway Hills (October 26, 2025), and 119 at Needwood (August 29, 2025).

- [Golf](https://rburke.dev/#golf)
